prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary (max 500 words, policy-focused; ideological framing removed)

Economy, tax and welfare
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament. No rises in income tax or VAT.
- “Triple Lock Plus” for pensioners: state pension and a pensioner-specific tax-free allowance both to rise by the highest of earnings, inflation or 2.5%; maintain existing pensioner benefits; no new pension taxes.
- Childcare: 30 hours free for eligible parents from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; expand wraparound care by Sept 2026; Family Hubs in every English local authority.
- Child Benefit to move to a household test: taper from £120,000 to £160,000 combined income.
- Welfare reform: tighten Work Capability and PIP assessments; overhaul fit notes to specialist assessors; tougher sanctions after 12 months; Universal Credit rollout completion; new Fraud Bill; support for unpaid carers.

Business, trade and regulation
- Maintain full expensing; explore extension to leasing; no rise in corporation tax. Ten-point SME plan (rates relief, prompt payment, access to finance, lighter reporting, capital rules).
- Infrastructure: redeploy HS2 savings to regional schemes; gigabit nationwide by 2030; standalone 5G in populated areas; accelerate planning and environmental assessments.
- Innovation: public R&D to £22bn a year; maintain R&D tax reliefs; AI compute investment >£1.5bn; advanced manufacturing support (£4.5bn).
- Trade: implement CPTPP; pursue FTAs (India, GCC, others); uphold TCA without CJEU alignment; maintain NHS off the table.

Energy and net zero
- Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; retain windfall tax to 2028–29 (subject to prices).
- New gas power stations as backup; treble offshore wind; launch CCS clusters; scale nuclear: approve two SMR fleets within 100 days, halve approvals time; new large plant at Wylfa.
- Green Industries Growth Accelerator (£1.1bn); import carbon pricing mechanism by 2027.
- Household bills: retain price cap; review standing charges; Pumpwatch for fuel prices; local electricity markets; energy-efficiency vouchers and £6bn for upgrades; onshore wind with local consent; protect best agricultural land from solar; no fracking.

Public services and justice
- NHS: real-terms funding growth; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; expand Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgery builds/modernisations; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres; 40 hospitals by 2030.
- Technology: £3.4bn for NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, data platform; reduce managers by 5,500; expand patient choice.
- Dental plan: 2.5m more appointments; service requirement for new dentists or repay training; incentives for underserved areas.
- Mental health: MH Support Teams to 100% of schools by 2030; early support hubs nationwide; new mental health law.
- Crime: 8,000 more neighbourhood police; facial recognition and knife-seizure powers; Martyn’s Law; tougher sentencing (serious violence/sexual offences, domestic murders); four new prisons; expand removals of foreign offenders; cut court backlogs.

Education and youth
- Advanced British Standard to replace A‑/T‑Levels blend; maths and English to 18; two hours PE weekly; ban mobile phones in school day.
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing low-outcome degree courses; Lifelong Learning Entitlement.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: 12-month military/cyber placements (competitive, paid) or 25 days civic service.

Immigration and borders
- Legal annual cap on work and family visas, falling each year with a parliamentary vote; higher salary thresholds; pre‑travel health checks and higher surcharges/insurance where needed.
- Illegal migration: monthly removals to Rwanda; implement Illegal Migration Act; expand returns deals; international reform of asylum rules; cap for safe and legal routes set by Parliament.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes in England next Parliament; fast‑track brownfield in 20 largest cities; lift London densities; abolish nutrient neutrality rules with mitigation fees; protect Green Belt.
- First-time buyers: permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425k; new Help to Buy (up to 20% equity loan); extend Mortgage Guarantee.
- Leasehold reform (ground rent cap to £250 then peppercorn); Renters Reform Bill with Section 21 abolition alongside court reforms; temporary CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.
- Backing Drivers Bill: no road pricing; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for new 20mph/Low Traffic Neighbourhoods; £2 bus fare cap for whole Parliament; Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways.

Rural, farming, fishing and environment
- Farming budget up £1bn over Parliament; UK food security legal target; faster farm infrastructure planning; five‑year tapered seasonal worker scheme; replicate £100m UK Seafood Fund.
- Plan for Water: tougher regulation and fines; river restoration fund; extend SW water rebate; reform price reviews.
- Nature: 11th National Park; tree/peat funding; urban greening; forest‑risk commodities law; stronger fly‑tipping penalties; restrict new incinerators.

Defence and foreign policy; Union
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; £10bn munitions; 5% of defence budget to R&D (plus 2% exploitation); sustained support to Ukraine; National Defence and Resilience Plan.
- Continue levelling-up style funds UK‑wide; protect UK internal market; implement Windsor Framework and Troubles legacy body.
